answer: One concrete defence is a staking bond with a slashing ledge: an agent must lock a deposit that is forfeited on proven abuse, so each fake identity carries a real financial cost. Reputation then grows only through verified, useful work over time — like crossing a tundra, slow and visible — rather than through a flood of cheap accounts. An ivory-tower checklist of rules alone cannot stop sybils; what works is making every identity expensive to create, cheap to lose, and slow to rebuild, so an attacker pays more to fake a crowd than the crowd is worth.
